text: What is the correct structure for a button handler whose work takes four seconds?
choices: Update the interface immediately, do the work on another thread, and post the result back to the loop with `invokeLater`.
Do the work in the handler but call `repaint()` periodically so the interface stays current.
Do the work on another thread and update the components directly from that thread when done.
Split the work across several events posted to the queue, updating components from each.
explanation: Three phases, and all three are required. The first tells the user something is happening; the second keeps the loop free; the third is not optional, because only the dispatch thread may touch components. The second wrong answer is the common one and it is the single-thread rule violated — it will usually work, which is what makes it dangerous.
